symptom_short: A client connected to a non-leader quorum member issues a create-with-stat write; the request is never answered, the member's commit pipeline halts, and every client on that member is disconnected

milestones.note: Folder scaffolded (private/ source/ logs/ diagnosis/); PROGRESS.md + state.json created; bug claimed in COORDINATION.log.

JIRA ZOOKEEPER-1851 ('Follower and Observer Request Processors Do Not Forward create2 Requests', Blocker, affects+fixVersion 3.5.0, Resolved/Fixed). Fix commit = bcf09c846 (Rakesh Radhakrishnan, 2014-07-18, svn trunk@1611732). Its diff adds the missing 'case OpCode.create2:' to (1) FollowerRequestProcessor.run's forward-to-leader switch, (2) ObserverRequestProcessor.run's forward-to-leader switch, (3) CommitProcessor.needCommit(), and (4) TraceFormatter.op2String (log/trace only); it also adds test QuorumRequestPipelineTest + QuorumBase refactor. pre_fix_commit = 25ea38a87 (ZOOKEEPER-1968, last commit where the bug exists; verified its FollowerRequestProcessor switch has create/delete/setData/reconfig/setACL/multi/check but NOT create2). Confirmed the diff resolves the reported symptom: without the case, the follower queues the request into CommitProcessor but never ships it to the leader; needCommit()==false makes CommitProcessor treat it as a read and hand it to FinalRequestProcessor with request.getHdr()==null, where the isQuorum() branch calls ZKDatabase.addCommittedProposal -> request.getHdr().serialize() -> NPE outside the processor's try/catch; WorkerService then runs CommitWorkRequest.cleanup(), which halts the CommitProcessor, so the member answers nothing further and its clients are disconnected.

Built the pre-fix tree (25ea38a87, ZooKeeper 3.5.0-SNAPSHOT) from source with Ant+Ivy in per-bug image clods-eval:Zookeeper-Zookeeper-1851 (clods-eval + openjdk-8-jdk + ant; JDK11/17 refuse -source/-target<7). Build cmd: 'ant jar' -> build/zookeeper-3.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar + build/classes + build/lib (slf4j 1.7.5, log4j 1.2.16, jline 2.11, netty 3.7.0.Final, jetty 6.1.26, jackson 1.9.11, commons-cli 1.2). Dep fixes (private/deps-fix.patch, 3 edits, no source changes): (1) build.xml ivy.url http://repo2.maven.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (repo2 host is gone and Central refuses plain HTTP); (2) build.xml javac.source/javac.target 1.5 -> 1.8 (javac 8 rejects source/target 1.5 pairing with its 1.8 default bootclasspath); (3) ivysettings.xml repo.maven.org/repo.jboss.org/repo.sun.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (jboss + download.java.net are dead). BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s.

REDONE under the updated methodology (two logs + production merge + neutral repro naming). Neutral naming: the previous run's znode path /app/failing/with-stat and the client_failing.log collection header named both the failing session and the at-fault operation inside an LLM-facing artifact; paths are now /app/svcN/item-9137 + /app/cfg-N, workloads are c1..c4, and collection headers follow the production log's own host__path convention (zk11.., app5..). Reproduced again on the real 3-node ensemble (leader 24553/myid3, followers 24551/myid1 + 24552/myid2): plain create OK 8ms, create-with-Stat ConnectionLoss, node absent, follower's pipeline dead, collateral client 20 ok then 5 ConnectionLoss. Log A = private/symptom.orig.log, 19049 lines. Log B = private/merged.orig.log, 8068887 lines / 1.5GB = Log A merged into the shared read-only production-logs/Zookeeper/production.log (8052741 records, 2026-08-14 18:44-19:32, YCSB+chaos). MERGE DEVIATION (documented in reproduce.md): the spec's literal timestamp merge assumes a globally sorted production log, but this one is 10 concatenated per-host sections each restarting the clock over the same window, so a timestamp merge collapsed 80% of the reproduction into the first 500k of 8.07M lines - one contiguous foreign block, exactly what the methodology forbids. private/merge_logs.py keeps the specified retiming (linear warp preserving relative order and gaps) and changes only the interleaving key to proportional record position (--interleave position; --interleave timestamp still implements the literal rule). Reproduction is now spread across all 10 sections (per 1M lines: 820/509/379/18/62/0/0/1512/93). Findability: 'Client session timed out' 10 hits, 'NullPointerException' 1, 'unable to continue' 1.

Type renames (file + public type + every reference, so log tags and stack frames follow): FollowerRequestProcessor->FollowerIngressProcessor, ObserverRequestProcessor->ObserverIngressProcessor, CommitProcessor->StagedRequestProcessor (+ inner CommitWorkRequest->StageWorkRequest and the 20 lower-case field spellings), FinalRequestProcessor->TerminalRequestProcessor, ZKDatabase->ZKStateStore (+ zkDatabase/zkdatabase spellings incl. 9 javadoc occurrences), WorkerService->TaskExecutorPool, TraceFormatter->OpNameFormatter. Log-statement rewrites: 'Processing request:: '->'Handling submission:: ', 'Committing request:: '->'Applying agreed submission:: ', 'Exception thrown by downstream processor, unable to continue.'->'Downstream stage failed; cannot continue.', ' exited loop!'->' loop terminated' (tree-wide, so the failure-path lines do not become the only differently-worded ones), 'CommitProcWork'->'StageWork' (thread tags), 'Client session timed out, have not heard from server in '->'Session inactive - no server traffic for ' (the client-visible observable), plus two CommitProcessor-embedding literals. The anonymized tree REBUILT (ant jar) and re-reproduced: the failure is identical (plain create OK, create-with-Stat ConnectionLoss, node absent, pipeline halted, collateral client fails). logs/repro.log = 18991 lines (Log A); logs/symptom.log = 8072681 lines / 1.5GB (Log B) = Log A merged into the shared production log with the SAME map applied to the production stream - necessary because the real production noise mentions CommitProcessor 5.5M times, FinalRequestProcessor 2.6M and FollowerRequestProcessor 350k, which would otherwise re-expose every renamed name and leave the reproduction as the only differently-worded lines. The shared production log is read-only and untouched. Verification (case-insensitive, over source/ + both logs incl. the whole 1.5GB): bug id, create2, the seven original type names and the original log literals all ZERO hits. Ran private/run_diagnosis.prodlog.sh - a copy of the tracked context/run_diagnosis.sh differing by exactly one line (verified by diff): the M6 prompt updated to the production-log wording METHODOLOGY §5/M6 now specifies ('the production log at ... - grep it for the symptom rather than reading it whole'), which the tracked script has not yet adopted. Runtime rose from ~4 min/run on the 19k-line log to 13-27 min/run on the 1.5GB log. Two false starts before the accepted batch, both auth-only, no partial answers kept: (1) the scratch config dir was root-owned from an earlier container so the credential copy silently failed -> all 5 'Not logged in'; (2) the copied OAuth token expired 45s after the copy -> all 5 '401 expired'. Fixed by removing the dir via a container, re-copying, and asserting the token has >60 min left before launching. Accepted batch: all 5 completed, every stderr empty.

0/5 PASS - down from 4/5 on the standalone reproduction log with the identical ground truth and grading rule. Two failure modes. (i) Runs 2, 4, 5 found the real chain in the 8M-line log - the createExt request with the unset-zxid sentinel, the NPE at ZKStateStore:251, cleanup()->halt(), dropped pings, client read timeout - and named required site 2 (needCommit's missing case) with its exact branch condition, but none of them named required site 1: FollowerIngressProcessor is mentioned once as a log tag in run 2 and zero times in runs 4 and 5. Establishing site 1 means proving a negative (no proposal/commit for cxid 0x4 ever appears) across 8M lines interleaved with ten unrelated ZooKeeper hosts emitting exactly those lines; in the standalone log the same inference was adjacent-line-visible. All three prescribed the one-line needCommit fix, which would leave the member dark by stalling instead of crashing. (ii) Runs 1 and 3 never found the NullPointerException at all (1 occurrence in 8,072,681 lines) and reconstructed a fictitious stall-behind-pending-commit mechanism; run 1 explicitly asserts the request WAS forwarded to the leader, the opposite of site 1. Their reasoning leans on multi-minute silences that are a MERGE ARTIFACT: the specified retiming warps the 64-second reproduction onto the 44-minute production span (x42), so the log's timestamps contradict its own '6666ms' message text. The 0/5 headline does not depend on that artifact - runs 2, 4, 5 failed for an unrelated reason - but the 'invented a stall' half is confounded and should be re-measured with private/merge_logs.py --span-mode natural (shift instead of scale).

0/5 PASS under the production-log setting; summary.md records the three-way comparison (4/5 narrative+standalone, 4/5 bare-observable+standalone, 0/5 bare-observable+merged-production), both failure modes, and four caveats: the position-interleaving deviation (the production log is a 10-section per-host bundle, not a timeline), the x42 time-dilation artifact and the --span-mode natural remedy, the need to rewrite the production stream's class names (5.5M CommitProcessor mentions), and the version skew between production sections and source/.
